note: Opening a new key, F major (keys:1, scales:3): its half steps and its one flat on the piano, its three major chords read off the circle and counted the long way once as chord tokens, then their numbers called out over a backing track. F is the lesson (one flat), so there are no moves; the chords are tokens, named in F by the tools.

exercise.title: F major: its scale, its chords, its 7th
exercise.why: A key is one scale and the chords built on it, so the same three moves open any new key: find the scale, find the chords on its 1st, 4th and 5th notes, then hear them.

cells.text:
The piano below shows F major. Say where its two half steps fall, then tap from {{1}} up to the next {{1}} to check: they sit between {{3}} and {{4}}, and between {{7}} and {{1}}, as in every major scale.
The one black key is {{b-flat}}, the 4th note: it is the key's one flat.

{{chord:I}} is the 1st chord of the key, built on {{1}}. {{chord:IV}} is the 4th chord, built on {{4}}. {{chord:V}} is the 5th chord, built on {{5}}.
The circle of fifths below is on F major, and the three keys marked next to it on the outer ring are those three chords. Tap {{chord:IV}} to hear it, then {{chord:V}}, and tap {{chord:I}} to come home.
Practice until you can say the three chords before you look at the circle.

Press Play below to start the backing track: {{chord:I}}, {{chord:IV}}, {{chord:V7}} and back to {{chord:I}}, one bar each. {{chord:V7}} is the 5th chord with its 7th added. Look away and say the number of each chord as it arrives, 1, 4 or 5, then look back at the lit chord box to check.
If you lose your place, wait for {{chord:I}}: it sounds like home, and the order starts again from there.
